## (a) Where the package list is derived from, and what happens if it misses one

Every non-private workspace package, each at the version **its own manifest**
declares — 69 today; `--dry-run` prints them. Membership is not a fourth private
copy of the filter: it reuses `listWorkspacePackages` from
`scripts/release-github-releases.mjs`, the release lane's existing answer to
"which packages are publishable", itself built on
`scripts/workspace-enumerator.mjs`, this repo's one parse of
`pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

I rejected the other permitted source — parsing `changeset publish`'s stdout —
**on the direction each fails in**, which is the whole argument. Parsing the
publisher's own report is self-referential: a publish that died early, printed
nothing, or changed its output format yields an **empty** parse, and the
verification then passes having checked nothing. That is the silent-success
direction, and it is the same class of bug this card is about. The workspace
derivation is independent of the publish's belief — it is the set that *ought*
to be on npm, computed from the tree the guard step already proved matches
`github.sha`.

**If it misses a package.** It cannot under-select against `changeset publish`,
whose own publishable set is the same workspace filter — a package outside the
workspace is not something this repo can publish at all. The one way it could
**over**-select is a future non-empty `.changeset/config.json` `ignore` (empty
today), and that direction is **loud**: the run reds naming that package, within
one release, instead of passing in silence. Two existing gates keep it honest and
neither is this one: `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` runs in this same job before the
build and asserts every non-private workspace package is in the Changesets
`fixed` group, and a package this repo does not publish is marked
`private: true` in its own manifest — exactly the field the filter reads.

Vacuity is guarded separately, because "everything published is readable" is
worth nothing when the derivation quietly yields nothing: an empty target set is
a hard failure, and so is a set missing `@objectstack/cli` — one anchor whose
absence means the derivation broke rather than that the workspace shrank, chosen
because it is the package this workflow audits, names on the approval screen and
reads out of the object database.

## (b) The two readings — old red, new green

Reproduced without npm. The self-test drives the **real** code against a stub
registry whose read path settles (a package committed but answering absent for
its first N reads), and expresses the **old** shape as *parameters of the same
function* — `targets: [cli]`, `budgetMs: 0` — so the old behaviour is pinned by
this code rather than by a second implementation nothing holds to it.

**Reading ① — the false red, and it absorbed.** With one cold read on `cli` (the
7-second gap measured on 17.3.0), the old shape returns
`ok: false`, `missing: [@objectstack/cli@17.3.0]`, having read the registry
exactly once — a red naming the package that was fine. The same stub under the
new parameters returns `ok: true` after backoff, with all three targets checked.

**Reading ② — the masked defect, and it caught.** With `@objectstack/runtime`
never landing and `cli` readable immediately, the old shape returns `ok: true` —
and never even asked about `runtime`. The new shape returns `ok: false` naming
`@objectstack/runtime` and nothing else, and probes `cli` exactly once across
all rounds because retries only re-probe what is still missing.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`, **not** an empty changeset — an empty one is rejected by #5471
and is itself the silently-green publish blocker of #4898. `.github/workflows/**`
and `scripts/**` publish nothing from any package, which is the label's own
stated condition ("PR has no user-facing published change").

The additive REST endpoint was unreachable from this container (repo-scoped REST
403, `gh` absent), so I declare the channel switch: the label went through MCP as
a whole-set write of `union(read, {skip-changeset})`, issued **after** the size
labeler had already run (it stamped `size/xl` at 12:05:21, the PR was created at
12:05:02), and then read back comparatively — read-back is
`["size/xl", "skip-changeset"]`, equal to the union, nothing stripped. Flagging
one contract conflict rather than silently picking a side: the dispatch reserved
this label for the PM, while the standing os-dev contract makes it my step at
PR-open time. I applied it, because a re-application is an idempotent no-op and
waiting for Check Changeset to red is the failure the contract names.

⛔ No auto-merge armed — `release.yml` is the one file in this repository that
publishes.
